subject: A Rare Double Miss From JPMorgan
body_text:
Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: Shares plunge: Six Flags (FUN) cooperating with authorities after rollercoaster death. Moody's calculations: How much is the Iran war costing each U.S. household?On the move: Micron (MU) under $1000 after authorizing record share buyback.

 Good morning! Here's the latest in trending: 

 Shares plunge: Six Flags ( FUN ) cooperating with authorities after rollercoaster death . 

 Moody's calculations: How much is the Iran war costing each U.S. household? 

 On the move: Micron ( MU )  under $1000 after authorizing record share buyback .
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Top News
 
 
 
 Cautious tone 
 
 
 
Getty Images
 
 
 The Q3 earnings season is upon investors, as the big banks kick off the start to the festivities. Reporting this morning are JPMorgan Chase ( JPM ), Goldman Sachs ( GS ), Citigroup ( C ) and Wells Fargo ( WFC ). It doesn't end there, with Bank of America and Morgan Stanley ( MS ) scheduled to release their earnings on Wednesday.

 At the time of writing: So far... investors have been underwhelmed. Shares of JPMorgan ( JPM ) slipped 3.3% in premarket trading as the Jamie Dimon-led institution missed consensus estimates on the top and bottom lines. Driving the rare miss were a $658M net securities loss and a slowdown in investment banking. Wells Fargo ( WFC ) also fell 1.2% premarket as revenue and net interest income came in short , though growth extended across consumer banking and commercial segments . Note that post-earnings trading is often volatile and things can turn around as quickly as they started.

 "The U.S. economy continues to be fueled by strong business investment and ongoing consumer spending. However, large fiscal deficits, sticky inflation, elevated asset prices, rising interest rates and geopolitical conditions continue to shift under the surface," Dimon declared following the results. "These forces may be manageable, but we remain prepared for a wide range of outcomes."

 Stay tuned: Goldman Sachs ( GS ) and Citigroup ( C ) will report shortly, with conference calls for all the banking behemoths scheduled from 8:30 AM - 11:00 AM ET. CEOs and top brass will have to reassure shareholders, who have been worried in recent months over rising borrowing costs and inflation. There have also been concerns over what artificial intelligence will mean for the industry, as well as IPO uncertainty, as listings are put on ice in the current choppy environment.

 Billions continue to pour into chips, data centers, and AI infrastructure. But as the financing behind that investment grows more complex, questions are emerging about how sustainable the current pace may be.

 Join Steven Cress, VP of Quantitative Strategy, and Kevin M. Sanford, Quantitative Macro Strategist, as they examine the forces driving the AI boom, the risks emerging beneath the surface, and parallels with the late-1990s dot-com era .
